accuracy.evidence: Uses NC Year 1 wording for whole, half, quarter and three-quarter turns and Year 2 clockwise/anticlockwise; the lab's four facing directions match the quarter-turn count exactly.

misconceptions.evidence: Adult text names whole-turn-means-backwards, counting the start as a quarter, and clockwise/anticlockwise mix-ups; why() in the challenge replies to each of these slips.

lab_distinct.evidence: Whole-body turning of a character to face landmarks with a filling wedge; unlike the grid transformation lab (532) which rotates shapes about a point for ages 8-12.

lab_teaches.evidence: Each tap adds one quarter of a visible wedge and Pip's facing changes, so the size of the turn is seen and counted before the words half and three-quarter are used.

predictions.evidence: Four predictions (quarter, half as two quarters, three-quarter, whole turn) are checked against what Pip actually faces after the animation, with spot-on or rethink replies.

challenge_feedback.evidence: Seven challenge questions mix clockwise and anticlockwise; wrong answers get a reason tied to counting quarter turns, plus a Show me replay on Pip.

readability.evidence: Kid paragraphs use stand-up-and-turn body actions with short sentences and Year 1 words; adult paragraphs give curriculum terms and the exact mistakes.

no_filler.evidence: Every paragraph either defines a turn size, the clock direction words, or a named mistake; there are no generic motivational lines in kid or adult text.

mobile.evidence: iPhone 13 screenshots in light and dark show large young-mode buttons for clockwise, anticlockwise and Start again under a square canvas with no overflow.

accessibility.evidence: Every turn is available by button as well as drag; the canvas aria-label states Pip's facing and the turn so far, and walk.cjs axe passed in both themes.

sources: UK National Curriculum 2013, Year 1 Geometry: position and direction
UK National Curriculum 2013, Year 2 Geometry: position and direction (clockwise, anticlockwise, right angles)
NCETM Year 1/2 position and direction guidance
